ety.text: From French hydraulique, from Latin hydraulicus, from Ancient Greek ὑδραυλικός (hudraulikós, “of a water organ”), from ὕδραυλις (húdraulis, “water organ”), from ὕδωρ (húdōr, “water”) + αὐλός (aulós, “pipe”).

senses.d: Related to, or operated by, hydraulics.
ex: A hydraulic press is operated by the differential pressure of water on pistons of different dimensions.

senses.d: To mine using the technique of hydraulic mining.

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Latin hyraulicus, from Ancient Greek ὑδραυλικός (hudraulikós).

From Latin hydraulicus, from Ancient Greek ὑδραυλικός (hudraulikós, “of a water organ”), from ὕδραυλις (húdraulis, “water organ”), from ὕδωρ (húdōr, “water”) + αὐλός (aulós, “pipe”). Cognate with Piedmontese idràulich.

senses.d: The lightest chemical element (symbol H), with an atomic number of 1 and atomic weight of 1.008.
ex: Our professor then reminded us that a hydrogen ion is merely a proton, and thus we should think about acid-base theory as we consider this problem further.
Each carbon of the ring has one hydrogen attached except for the fourth one, which is bonded to a substituent.

senses.d: Molecular hydrogen (sense 1; symbol H₂), a colourless, odourless and flammable gas at room temperature.
ex: A large tank of hydrogen constituted most of the bulk of that rocket.

senses.d: A molecule of this molecular species.
Synonym of protium (“the lightest and most common isotope of hydrogen (sense 1; symbol H, ¹H, or 11H), as contrasted with deuterium and tritium”).
ex: Both hydrogen and deuterium are present in every glass of water that you drink, but the amount of deuterium is rather small.

ety.text: From hydro- + -gène. Coined by French nobleman and chemist Antoine Lavoisier in 1783.
From French hydrogène. By surface analysis, idro- (“water”) + -geno (“producer”).

Borrowed from French hydrogène. Coined by Lavoisier and his team, from Ancient Greek ὑδρο- (hudro-, “water”) (from ὕδωρ (húdōr, “water”)) + -γενής (-genḗs, “producer of”) (from γεννάω (gennáō, “to bring forth”)). By surface analysis, hidro- + -geno.
